dimensions: the user's path and the design
reasoning: The transition engine is being built right now, and this message changes a constraint on that work: whatever the engine produces must move, never sit still. That is a correction — it attaches to the work already in flight, so its goal and the remainder of its plan get replanned on the checkpoint that work already has, and no second row opens beside it. It is one act: there is a single clause, with no separate grounds saying anything the constraint does not already carry, and nothing here reads as a standing rule beyond this piece of work — mid-implementation of exactly this thing, the absolute wording is the constraint on it, not a rule that outlives it. The corrected work touches product value and behaviour (what a transition does changes), the user's path and the design (the experience of moving between states is the thing being judged), and quality (something has to catch a static transition before it ships). It needs the developer to rebuild the engine to that constraint, the design reviewer because the coherence of the motion is what is being corrected, and the test author to choose the evidence that no static transition survives.
